title: Nehemiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nehemiah chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nehemiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nehemiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who did Nehemiah give charge over Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah gave his brother Hanani charge over Jerusalem, as stated in Nehemiah 7:2.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah instruct them to do with the gates of Jerusalem?
options: Keep them shut until it is hot
questions.correctAnswer: Keep them shut until it is hot
questions.explanation: Nehemiah instructed that the gates of Jerusalem should not be opened until the sun be hot, as stated in Nehemiah 7:3.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah found a register of the genealogy of those who came up at the first.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah found a register of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, as stated in Nehemiah 7:5.

questions.question: What was the condition of the city according to Nehemiah?
options: It was large and great but few people lived there
questions.correctAnswer: It was large and great but few people lived there
questions.explanation: Nehemiah described the city as large and great, but with few people therein, as stated in Nehemiah 7:4.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Parosh numbered two thousand one hundred seventy and two.
questions.explanation: The number of the children of Parosh was indeed two thousand one hundred seventy and two, as stated in Nehemiah 7:8.

questions.question: Which group was NOT mentioned in Nehemiah 7:7 as having come up?
questions.explanation: Ezra is not mentioned in Nehemiah 7:7; the verse lists other leaders who came up with Zerubbabel.

questions.question: What was the total number of the whole congregation together?
options: Forty-two thousand three hundred and threescore
questions.correctAnswer: Forty-two thousand three hundred and threescore
questions.explanation: The total number of the whole congregation was forty-two thousand three hundred and threescore, as stated in Nehemiah 7:66.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah mentions that there were more horses than mules.
questions.explanation: There were seven hundred thirty and six horses and two hundred forty and five mules, indicating there were more horses than mules, making the statement false.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 7, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Shut the gates until it is hot
questions.explanation: Nehemiah first mentions setting up the doors after the wall was built, as stated in Nehemiah 7:1.

questions.question: Which group had the smallest recorded number in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The children of Hariph had the smallest recorded number, which was an hundred and twelve, as stated in Nehemiah 7:24.

questions.question: True or False: The Levites numbered seventy and four according to Nehemiah.
questions.explanation: According to Nehemiah 7:43, the Levites, specifically the children of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, and of the children of Hodevah, numbered seventy and four.

medium.title: Nehemiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nehemiah Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the total number of men from the children of Senaah who returned?
questions.explanation: The total number of men from the children of Senaah who returned is recorded as three thousand nine hundred and thirty in Nehemiah 7:38.

questions.question: Which group of people had the least number of returnees listed in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The children of Bethazmaveth had the least number of returnees listed, with a count of forty and two in Nehemiah 7:28.

questions.question: How many priests are mentioned as the children of Jedaiah in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, are recorded as nine hundred seventy and three in Nehemiah 7:39.

questions.question: The men of which city had the highest count of returnees?
questions.explanation: The children of Senaah had the highest count of returnees, totaling three thousand nine hundred and thirty as noted in Nehemiah 7:38.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 7:66 state about the whole congregation?
questions.explanation: The whole congregation together was stated to be forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore in Nehemiah 7:66.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 7:45, how many porters returned?
questions.explanation: The number of porters listed is one hundred thirty and eight in Nehemiah 7:45.

questions.question: True or False: The children of the other Elam numbered 1,254.
questions.explanation: The children of the other Elam are specifically mentioned as numbering a thousand two hundred fifty and four in Nehemiah 7:34, making the statement true.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah gave charge over Jerusalem to Hananiah because he was unfaithful.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah appointed Hananiah over Jerusalem because he was a faithful man and feared God above many, as stated in Nehemiah 7:2, making the statement false.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 7:71 reveal about the chief of the fathers?
options: They gave gold and silver to the treasure.
They built the walls of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: They gave gold and silver to the treasure.
questions.explanation: The verse describes how some of the chief of the fathers gave to the treasure of the work, including gold and silver, as indicated in Nehemiah 7:71.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 7:63 connect with the priesthood?
options: They were permitted to eat the holy things.
They were put from the priesthood.
questions.correctAnswer: They were put from the priesthood.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 7:64 states that those who could not show their genealogy were put from the priesthood as they were considered polluted, connecting their genealogy with their ability to serve.

questions.question: What biblical principle does Nehemiah 7 teach about obedience to leadership?
options: It shows the importance of following godly leaders.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of following godly leaders.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah's appointments and instructions demonstrate the importance of recognizing and obeying godly leaders who guide the community, as shown throughout the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: The total number of returnees from the children of Harim was 1,017.
questions.explanation: The number of returnees from the children of Harim is indeed stated as one thousand and seventeen in Nehemiah 7:42, making the statement true.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 7 reflect the theme of community and support among the Israelites?
options: It divides the people into separate factions.
It shows the people returning as individuals.
It emphasizes their collective return and contributions.
It discourages unity among the tribes.
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes their collective return and contributions.
questions.explanation: The detailed accounts of returnees and their contributions showcase the unity and collective effort of the Israelites in rebuilding Jerusalem, highlighting the importance of community.

hard.title: Nehemiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nehemiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the ruler over Jerusalem by Nehemiah?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah appointed Hananiah as the ruler over Jerusalem because he was a faithful man and feared God above many (Nehemiah 7:2).

questions.question: What did Nehemiah instruct regarding the gates of Jerusalem?
options: To keep them open all day
To shut them until the sun is hot
To leave them open at night
questions.correctAnswer: To shut them until the sun is hot
questions.explanation: Nehemiah instructed that the gates should not be opened until the sun was hot and that they should be shut and barred (Nehemiah 7:3).

questions.question: What was the reason for gathering the nobles and rulers according to Nehemiah?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah gathered the nobles and rulers so that they might be reckoned by genealogy, as indicated by God's prompting in his heart (Nehemiah 7:5).

questions.question: How many children of Zattu came back from captivity?
questions.explanation: The children of Zattu numbered eight hundred forty and five who returned from captivity (Nehemiah 7:13).

questions.question: What does the term 'Nethinims' refer to in the context of Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The Nethinims were designated as servants of the temple, as described in Nehemiah 7:60, where they are listed among the people.

questions.question: How many total men, including servants, returned to Jerusalem according to Nehemiah?
questions.explanation: The total congregation that returned to Jerusalem was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore (Nehemiah 7:66).

questions.question: Which biblical theme does Nehemiah’s concern for genealogy echo from earlier texts?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah's emphasis on genealogy parallels earlier texts in the Pentateuch, where lineage and priestly roles are crucial (e.g., Exodus 28:1).

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah indicated that the priests who could not prove their genealogy were allowed to serve in the priesthood.
questions.explanation: Those who could not prove their genealogy were put from the priesthood, indicating strict adherence to lineage requirements (Nehemiah 7:64).

questions.question: What did the Tirshatha say regarding the most holy things?
options: They could be eaten by anyone
They should not be eaten until a priest appears
They are reserved for the king
questions.correctAnswer: They should not be eaten until a priest appears
questions.explanation: The Tirshatha instructed that they should not eat of the most holy things until there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim (Nehemiah 7:65).

questions.question: What was the total number of Nethinims mentioned in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The total number of Nethinims and the children of Solomon's servants was three hundred ninety and two (Nehemiah 7:60).

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah's chapter ends with the people dwelling in their cities in the seventh month.
questions.explanation: The chapter concludes with all Israel dwelling in their cities when the seventh month came (Nehemiah 7:73).

questions.question: Which group of people were listed as having given significantly to the work?
questions.explanation: The chief of the fathers contributed significantly to the work, as noted in their giving to the treasure for the project (Nehemiah 7:70).

questions.question: What was the Hebrew meaning of 'Nethinim' as used in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: 'Nethinim' is derived from a Hebrew root meaning 'to give' or 'to serve', referring to those appointed as temple servants (Nehemiah 7:60).

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in the list of genealogies in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The genealogical lists employ repetition to emphasize the continuity of Israel's heritage, a common device in Hebrew literature (Nehemiah 7:7-8).

theological.title: Nehemiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nehemiah Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah appoint to guard the gates of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah instructed to appoint watches of the inhabitants to guard the gates until the sun was hot (Nehemiah 7:3).

questions.question: Who did Nehemiah give charge over Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah gave his brother Hanani and Hananiah charge over Jerusalem because Hananiah was a faithful man who feared God (Nehemiah 7:2).

questions.question: What was the condition of the city of Jerusalem as described in Nehemiah 7?
options: It was large but had few people
questions.correctAnswer: It was large but had few people
questions.explanation: Nehemiah noted that the city was large and great, but the people were few (Nehemiah 7:4).

questions.question: What does Nehemiah find that God put in his heart to do?
options: To gather the nobles for genealogy
questions.correctAnswer: To gather the nobles for genealogy
questions.explanation: God put it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the nobles and rulers to be reckoned by genealogy (Nehemiah 7:5).

questions.question: What was the total number of the congregation mentioned in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The whole congregation together was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore (Nehemiah 7:66).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Nehemiah's appointment of Hananiah?
questions.explanation: Hananiah is described as a faithful man, reflecting God's attribute of faithfulness in appointing leaders (Nehemiah 7:2).

questions.question: How does Nehemiah's gathering of the people connect to the overarching narrative of redemption?
options: It shows God's abandonment of Israel
It emphasizes the restoration of God's people
It indicates the end of Israel's significance
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the restoration of God's people
questions.explanation: Nehemiah's actions reflect God's commitment to restore His people after captivity, a key theme in the redemptive narrative (Nehemiah 7:5).

questions.question: What does the list of names in Nehemiah 7 signify?
questions.explanation: The names listed in Nehemiah 7 are part of the genealogy of those who returned from captivity, signifying their heritage (Nehemiah 7:6).

questions.question: What was the reason some priests could not show their genealogy?
options: They did not come from Israel
They were not of the right tribe
questions.explanation: The priests sought their register among those reckoned by genealogy, but it was not found, thus they were put from the priesthood (Nehemiah 7:64).

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 7 connect to the doctrine of ecclesiology?
options: It shows the independence of the church
It emphasizes the unity and order within the community
It disregards the need for leadership
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the unity and order within the community
questions.explanation: Nehemiah appoints leaders and organizes the people, reflecting the importance of order and unity in the body of believers (Nehemiah 7:2-3).

questions.question: What does the term 'Nethinims' refer to in Nehemiah 7?
questions.explanation: The Nethinims were a group of temple servants designated for the work of the temple (Nehemiah 7:46).

questions.question: What does Nehemiah's instruction to not eat of the most holy things imply about priestly conduct?
questions.explanation: The instruction implies that a priest must be properly recognized through genealogy to partake in the most holy things (Nehemiah 7:65).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that genealogies in the Bible are irrelevant. What does Nehemiah 7 actually teach?
options: They show God's faithfulness in preserving His people
questions.correctAnswer: They show God's faithfulness in preserving His people
questions.explanation: The genealogies demonstrate God's ongoing covenant relationship with His people and the importance of their identities (Nehemiah 7:6).

questions.question: What significant action did some of the chief fathers take in Nehemiah 7?
options: They provided resources for the work
questions.correctAnswer: They provided resources for the work
questions.explanation: The chief fathers contributed significantly to the resources for rebuilding and supporting the community (Nehemiah 7:70-72).

questions.question: How is the concept of stewardship illustrated in Nehemiah 7?
options: By the giving of resources to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: By the giving of resources to the temple
questions.explanation: The contributions made by the chief fathers and the people illustrate stewardship towards God's work (Nehemiah 7:70-72).
